=== installation.md
> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.entire.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Installation

> Install, update, verify, and uninstall the Entire CLI.

## System Requirements

* macOS, Linux, or Windows
* Git 2.25 or later
* Bash, Zsh, Fish, or PowerShell
* Windows PowerShell 5.1 or later, for the Windows PowerShell installer

Building from source requires Go 1.27.3 or later.

## Release Channels

Entire ships two release channels:

* `stable`: the default channel for Homebrew, Scoop, `install.sh`, and `install.ps1`
* `nightly`: prerelease builds available through Homebrew, `install.sh`, and `install.ps1`

Scoop supports the stable channel only. For a nightly install on Windows, use `install.ps1`.

## Install and Update Entire

Choose one installation method. Use the update command in the same tab when you want a newer release.

> [tab] macOS with Homebrew
>
> Install the stable channel:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire
> ```
>
> Or install the nightly channel:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire@nightly
> ```
>
> The fully qualified cask name adds the `entireio/tap` tap for you, so no separate `brew tap` step is needed.
>
> Update the channel you installed:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> brew upgrade --cask entireio/tap/entire
> ```
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> brew upgrade --cask entireio/tap/entire@nightly
> ```

> [tab] Linux Install Script
>
> Install the stable channel:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash
> ```
>
> Or install the nightly channel:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
> ```
>
> The script installs `entire` and `git-remote-entire` in `~/.local/bin`. If that directory is missing from your `PATH`, the script prints the command that adds it to your shell configuration.
>
> Run the command for your channel again to update Entire.

> [tab] Linux Direct Download
>
> Download the stable AMD64 archive and install both executables:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> download_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
> mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
> curl -fsSL https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/latest/download/entire_linux_amd64.tar.gz \
>   -o "$download_dir/entire_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
> tar -xzf "$download_dir/entire_linux_amd64.tar.gz" -C "$download_dir"
> install -m 0755 "$download_dir/entire" "$download_dir/git-remote-entire" "$HOME/.local/bin/"
> rm -rf "$download_dir"
> ```
>
> For ARM64, replace `amd64` with `arm64` in the archive name:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> download_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
> mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
> curl -fsSL https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/latest/download/entire_linux_arm64.tar.gz \
>   -o "$download_dir/entire_linux_arm64.tar.gz"
> tar -xzf "$download_dir/entire_linux_arm64.tar.gz" -C "$download_dir"
> install -m 0755 "$download_dir/entire" "$download_dir/git-remote-entire" "$HOME/.local/bin/"
> rm -rf "$download_dir"
> ```
>
> Run the block for your architecture again to update Entire.

> [tab] Windows with PowerShell
>
> Install the stable channel from Windows PowerShell 5.1 or later:
>
> ```powershell theme={null}
> irm https://entire.com/install.ps1 | iex
> ```
>
> Or install the nightly channel:
>
> ```powershell theme={null}
> iex "& {$(irm https://entire.com/install.ps1)} -Channel nightly"
> ```
>
> For the stable channel, the script uses Scoop when Scoop is on your `PATH`, and it adds the Entire bucket first. Without Scoop, and for every nightly install, the script verifies the release checksum, installs `entire.exe` and `git-remote-entire.exe` in `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`, and adds that directory to your user `PATH`. Restart your terminal after the script changes your `PATH`.
>
> The script accepts these options. Pass them with the script block form shown for the nightly channel, because `irm | iex` cannot forward arguments:
>
> | Option | Effect |
> | - | - |
> | `-Channel` | Release channel to install, `stable` or `nightly`. Defaults to `stable`. |
> | `-InstallDir` | Destination for a checksum verified install. Defaults to `$HOME\.local\bin`. Passing it selects the release archive even when Scoop is available. |
> | `-NoPathUpdate` | Leave your user `PATH` unchanged. Applies to release archive installs, because Scoop manages its own `PATH` entry. |
> | `-Help` | Print the usage message. |
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > In Git Bash, MSYS, or Cygwin, `install.sh` stops and points you to this installer.
>
> Run the command for your channel again to update Entire.

> [tab] Windows with Scoop
>
> These commands drive Scoop directly. The PowerShell installer already uses Scoop for stable installs when Scoop is available.
>
> Add the Entire bucket once, then install the stable channel:
>
> ```powershell theme={null}
> scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
> scoop install entire/entire
> ```
>
> Update Scoop and Entire:
>
> ```powershell theme={null}
> scoop update
> scoop update entire
> ```

# Set Up an Agent

> Install, verify, update, and remove Entire agent hooks

Entire installs repository-level hooks for each AI coding agent you use. Agent hooks capture session events, while Entire's Git hooks connect the captured session to commits.

## Before You Start

Install the [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.com/installation.md) and your preferred [agent integration](https://docs.entire.com/agents/overview.md). Run these commands from a Git repository after you enable Entire.

## Install Agent Hooks

Pass the integration's agent name to `entire agent add`:

```bash theme={null}
entire agent add AGENT_NAME
```

For example:

```bash theme={null}
entire agent add codex
```

You can install hooks for more than one agent in the same repository. Each integration keeps its configuration in the agent's project directory.

During initial Entire setup, select an agent with:

```bash theme={null}
entire enable --agent codex
```

## Agent Integrations

An agent integration adds support for a coding agent through an executable named `entire-agent-<name>`. A CLI plugin uses `entire-<name>` and adds a command instead. Add the agent integration executable to your `$PATH` and enable discovery in `.entire/settings.json`:

```json .entire/settings.json theme={null}
{
  "external_agents": true
}
```

Entire includes discovered integrations in `entire agent list`. During setup, pass the external agent's name without the `entire-agent-` prefix:

```bash theme={null}
entire enable --agent AGENT_NAME
```

See the [Agent Integration Protocol](https://docs.entire.com/agents/agent-integration-protocol/overview.md) for the protocol and its security considerations.

## Install CLI-Managed Skills

`entire agent add` can also install two repository-level skills:

```bash theme={null}
entire agent add codex --agent-help-skill --search-skill
```

| Flag | Installs |
| - | - |
| `--agent-help-skill` | A skill that directs the agent to `entire agent-help` for usage that matches the installed CLI |
| `--search-skill` | A skill that helps the agent run `entire search --json` |

These flags install the CLI-managed helpers. See [Install Skills](https://docs.entire.com/learn/skills-overview.md#install-skills) for the Entire Skills collection.

## Hook Locations

| Agent | Project Configuration |
| - | - |
| [Antigravity CLI](https://docs.entire.com/agents/antigravity.md) | `.agents/hooks.json` |
| Claude Code | `.claude/settings.json` |
| Codex | `.codex/hooks.json` |
| Copilot CLI | `.github/hooks/entire.json` |
| Cursor | `.cursor/hooks.json` |
| Factory | `.factory/settings.json` |
| OpenCode | `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` |
| Pi | `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` |

Entire preserves unrelated configuration when it adds JSON hooks. OpenCode and Pi use generated TypeScript files that Entire can reinstall when their templates change.

## Verify Capture

List the installed integrations and inspect the repository:

```bash theme={null}
entire agent list
entire status --detailed
```

Start a new agent session from the repository after installing hooks. Existing agent processes do not load hooks added after they started.

Commit a file change to create a checkpoint, then inspect it:

```bash theme={null}
git add .
git commit -m "Describe the change"
entire checkpoint list
```

See [Session Storage](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/checkpoint-storage.md) for where Entire writes checkpoint data.

## Reinstall or Remove Hooks

Reinstall missing, stale, or modified hooks with:

```bash theme={null}
entire agent add AGENT_NAME --force
```

Remove Entire's hooks for one integration with:

```bash theme={null}
entire agent remove AGENT_NAME
```

Removing one integration leaves other agent hooks and Entire's Git hooks in place.

## Troubleshoot Capture

Run `entire doctor` when `entire status --detailed` does not show a session you started. Confirm that the integration's configuration file exists, restart the agent, and run it from inside the repository.

Each agent page documents limitations on transcript capture, token usage, subagent capture, session resume, and transcript import. Use the [capability matrix](https://docs.entire.com/agents/overview.md#compare-built-in-integrations) to find the relevant page.

# Entire CLI and entire.com

> Mirror and clone your repos. Capture, inspect, search, and share the agent-work history recorded by Entire.

Entire has two ways to host your repositories and view your agent history:

* **Entire CLI.** Runs in your terminal and works with the repository on your machine. Use it to enable Entire in a repo, capture agent sessions, list and explain checkpoints, search past work, and create or clone mirrors.
* **[entire.com](https://entire.com).** The web interface for your repositories. Use it to browse, search, and share your agentic history and to connect GitHub repositories to Entire.

The CLI captures the work on your local machine as an agent works. When you commit and push, entire.com can read that captured history and make it easier to review with your team.

## Entire CLI

### What the Entire CLI Does

The Entire CLI captures your agent sessions and links them to your commits, so you and your agents can trace any change back to the work behind it. It also lets you clone and mirror your repositories directly from Entire. The Entire CLI helps you and your agent to:

* Record every agent session as a checkpoint linked to your commits, so the prompts, transcripts, and file changes behind a change are never lost.
* Search your code and the sessions, commits, and checkpoints behind it, from the terminal or from inside your agent.
* Explain why a file or line exists with `entire blame` and `entire why`, which show the checkpoint, prompt, and session that produced it.
* Mirror and clone your repositories natively on Entire, from the region closest to your agents.
* Hand off work between sessions and agents with the session handoff Skill and `entire session resume`, so the next agent starts with the context it needs.
* Review and summarize agent work with `entire review`, a multi-agent review of a branch, and `entire recap`, a summary of recent checkpoint activity.

For the full list of commands and features, see the [CLI Reference](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference).

### How to Access the CLI

[Install the CLI](https://docs.entire.com/installation.md), then run commands from inside a Git repository:

```bash theme={null}
entire version
entire status
```

Set up Entire for the coding agent you use:

```bash theme={null}
entire enable --yes --agent codex
```

Replace `codex` with your agent if needed, such as `claude-code` or `antigravity`. See [Set Up an Agent](https://docs.entire.com/agents/setup.md) for the full list.

These are some commands to start with:

```bash theme={null}
# See whether Entire is enabled and which sessions are active
entire status

# List checkpoints on the current branch
entire checkpoint list

# Explain the work behind a checkpoint or commit
entire checkpoint explain CHECKPOINT_ID
entire checkpoint explain HEAD~1

# See all recorded sessions, including ended ones
entire session list

# Search past agent work
entire search "how was authentication changed"
```

Some CLI commands use your hosted Entire account, such as cross-repository search, mirrors, and account activity. Sign in when prompted, or run:

```bash theme={null}
entire login
```

For a remote machine or container where a browser cannot open directly, use:

```bash theme={null}
entire login --device
```

### Host and Mirror Repositories from the CLI

Entire is a distributed Git hosting network. A [mirror](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirrors.md) is a synced copy of your GitHub repository that lives on Entire in a region you choose, so agents can clone and fetch from the cluster closest to them while GitHub stays the source of truth.

From the CLI you can create mirrors, see where a repository is mirrored, and clone or point an existing checkout at one:

```bash theme={null}
# List repositories you can mirror and mirrors that already exist
entire repo mirror list

# Register a mirror; Entire prompts for repositories and regions
entire repo mirror add

# Show each region, clone URL, and status for one repository
entire repo view /gh/OWNER/REPO

# Clone from the mirror
entire repo clone /gh/OWNER/REPO

# Add the mirror as a remote in an existing checkout
entire repo remote add entire
```

The [Entire GitHub App must have access to the repository](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/github-app-access.md) before you can create a mirror. If a repository is mirrored in more than one region, `entire repo clone` and `entire repo remote add` ask you to choose one. Without a terminal they fall back to `aws-us-east-2.entire.io` and error if the mirror is not placed there, so pass `--cluster` in scripts, or `entire repo clone --nearest` to pick the fastest.

Mirrors sync every push back to GitHub. To keep pushing when GitHub is down, or to absorb many agents pushing at once, push to an [Entire-native branch](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/entire-native-branches.md) by naming it with the `entire/unmirrored/` prefix. See [Mirrors in CLI](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirrors-in-cli.md) for the full command-line flow.

## entire.com

[entire.com](https://entire.com) is the browser-based view of the history the CLI captured. It is useful when you want a visual way to understand work, search across repositories, review your commits and work, or share context with teammates.

### What entire.com Shows

After you sign in, entire.com can show:

* Recent repository activity and commits.
* Checkpoints grouped by repository and branch.
* File diffs and the agent sessions that contributed to a checkpoint.
* Session timelines, prompts, transcripts, tool calls, and files.
* Search results for sessions, commits, checkpoints, and indexed source code.
* The repositories connected to your account, their mirror regions, and their GitHub App access.

![entire.com activity overview](https://mintcdn.com/entire/fgG56b7zcMZgFdOf/images/dashboard-repos-dark.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=fgG56b7zcMZgFdOf\&q=85\&s=96de0c2e6afed24444d677ce7d5fab64)

### How to Access entire.com

1. Install and enable the Entire CLI in the repository.
2. Commit and push your work so the checkpoint data is available to Entire.
3. Sign in at [entire.com](https://entire.com).
4. Open a repository, then choose a branch, checkpoint, session, or search result to inspect.

You do not need a local clone to review a repository in entire.com, but the repository must be connected to your Entire account and its data must be available.

### Host and Mirror Repositories in entire.com

entire.com is where you connect GitHub to Entire and choose which repositories Entire can see. The repository setup flow walks you through it:

1. **Configure GitHub App.** Install the Entire GitHub App, or update its access, for all repositories or only the ones you select. This step needs a GitHub organization admin if the repository belongs to an organization.
2. **Select repositories.** Choose the repositories to make available in Entire.
3. **Choose data residency.** Pick the region where Entire stores and serves each mirror. Entire currently offers regions in the United States, the European Union, the UK, India, Australia, and Brazil.

![GitHub repository mirrored across Entire regions in the United States, the European Union, the UK, India, Australia, and Brazil](https://mintcdn.com/entire/fKc-sQgYCHQiYiBO/images/mirrors-instant-repo-sync.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=fKc-sQgYCHQiYiBO\&q=85\&s=0c135a9bcbe0d59759db699be0eca839)

The mirrored repositories then appear in your repository list. Your team can browse their activity in entire.com, and agents can use each mirror as a regional Git remote with the `entire://` clone URL shown for it. Mirror access follows GitHub collaborator permissions and [syncs every hour](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirror-access-and-permissions.md).

See [Mirrors in entire.com](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirrors-in-entire-com.md) for the web flow with screenshots, or [Mirror a GitHub Repository](https://docs.entire.com/learn/mirror-a-github-repository.md) for the complete walkthrough from access setup through removal.

The two surfaces work together: the CLI captures and manages the history and creates mirrors from the terminal, while entire.com connects your GitHub repositories and makes that history easy to explore and share.

input.ask: How do you want to get past the Gatekeeper block on entire?

content.text:
Thanks for the screenshot. Click **Done** on that dialog, not "Move to Trash". The `entire` file itself is legitimate:

- **Signed:** it carries Entire Inc's Apple developer signature.
- **Matches the official release:** the file Homebrew installed is identical to the v0.13.1 download on GitHub (`entireio/cli`), checked by checksum.
- **Why macOS blocked it:** this release came out yesterday (Nov 6), and Apple hasn't approved it yet. Apple checks each release for malware before macOS will run it without a warning.

I won't get around this macOS security check myself, because it's your decision. If you want to run it now, either:
- go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down and click **Open Anyway** next to "entire", or
- run this in a terminal (it removes the block for this one file only):
```bash
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/entire/0.13.1/entire
```

The other option is to wait for a newer release that Apple has approved and update with `brew upgrade --cask entireio/tap/entire`.

Once it runs, I'll do this in the LouVoice repo:
1. **Turn on Entire for Claude Code:** `entire enable --agent claude-code`. This adds hooks to `.claude/settings.json`.
2. **Bring in our earlier work:** Entire can import Claude Code conversations from the last 30 days as read-only history. Anything older than that can't be imported.
3. **Sign in:** `entire login`, so the history shows up on entire.com. This opens a browser and needs you.
4. **Check it worked:** `entire status --detailed`.

You have uncommitted changes in four LouVoice files: `DECISIONS.md`, `AppModel.swift`, `Decoder.swift` and `Enrollment.swift`. I'll leave them alone. Entire won't link a session to code until you make a commit.

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.entire.com/llms.txt

# import

> Import pre-existing local agent transcripts as read-only checkpoints.

Import pre-existing local agent transcripts for the current repository as read-only checkpoints.

```bash theme={null}
entire import AGENT [flags]
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> `entire import` is experimental. It appears under **Experimental commands** in developer and nightly builds, but is hidden from top-level help in stable releases. It remains runnable in all builds and appears in [`entire labs`](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference/labs). Run `entire import --help` to see supported agents.

## Supported Agents

| Agent | Command |
| - | - |
| Claude Code | `entire import claude-code` |
| Codex | `entire import codex` |
| Copilot CLI | `entire import copilot-cli` |
| Cursor | `entire import cursor` |
| Factory | `entire import factoryai-droid` |
| Pi | `entire import pi` |

## Flags

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--dry-run` | Report what would be imported without writing checkpoints |
| `--path DIRECTORY` | Override the transcript directory to import from |
| `--session ID` | Import only this session ID. Repeatable. |

## Examples

Check what would be imported:

```bash theme={null}
entire import claude-code --dry-run
```

Import Claude Code transcript history:

```bash theme={null}
entire import claude-code
```

Import a specific Codex session:

```bash theme={null}
entire import codex --session SESSION_ID
```

Import from a custom transcript directory:

```bash theme={null}
entire import claude-code --path TRANSCRIPT_DIRECTORY
```

## Behavior

`entire import` scans the agent's local transcript store for the current repository and imports history from the past month.

Imported checkpoints are:

* read-only
* searchable
* explainable
* idempotent, so already-imported turns are skipped
* not rewindable
* not linked to a Git commit

# Import Past Sessions


Import past sessions when useful agent context exists locally, but Entire did not capture it while the work happened.

[Import existing Claude Code sessions demo](https://customer-0x5hsk8lh27fm00g.cloudflarestream.com/15376992270a4d75618e299a3fb8b1d8/iframe?muted=true\&loop=true\&autoplay=true\&poster=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-0x5hsk8lh27fm00g.cloudflarestream.com%2F15376992270a4d75618e299a3fb8b1d8%2Fthumbnails%2Fthumbnail.jpg%3Ftime%3D%26height%3D600)

## When to Import Past Sessions

Use `entire import` when:

* you enabled Entire after useful agent work already happened
* you want past local agent sessions to become searchable in Entire
* you want to import sessions from an agent's local transcript store

| If you want to | Use |
| - | - |
| Bring past local agent sessions into Entire | `entire import AGENT` |
| Link one missed session to the latest commit | [`entire session attach`](https://docs.entire.com/guides/sessions/attach-sessions) |
| Continue working from an earlier session | [`entire session resume`](https://docs.entire.com/guides/sessions/resume-sessions) |

## Preview an Import

Use `--dry-run` to see what Entire would import before writing checkpoints:

```bash theme={null}
entire import claude-code --dry-run
```

The preview shows how many sessions and turns Entire found, what would be imported, and what was already imported.

## Import Past Sessions

Import reads agent transcripts for the current repository, creates read-only checkpoints, and makes that history available in Entire.

Run import from inside the repository whose agent history you want to bring into Entire:

```bash theme={null}
entire import claude-code
```

Replace `claude-code` with the agent you want to import from. Run `entire import --help` or see the [import command reference](https://docs.entire.com/cli-reference/import.md) for supported agents and flags.

## Import Specific Sessions

Use `--session` when you only want to import a specific session:

```bash theme={null}
entire import claude-code --session SESSION_ID
```

You can repeat `--session` to import more than one session.

## Import from a Custom Transcript Path

Use `--path` when the agent transcripts are stored somewhere other than the default location:

```bash theme={null}
entire import claude-code --path TRANSCRIPT_DIRECTORY
```

## What Imported Sessions Become

Imported sessions are stored as read-only checkpoints in your repository's [checkpoint storage](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/checkpoint-storage.md), alongside the checkpoints Entire captures live.

Imported checkpoints are:

* searchable
* explainable
* idempotent, so re-running import skips turns that already exist
* not linked to a Git commit
* not rewindable
